result.body: Datasette transport, tape-sense, motor timing, and recording must reproduce pinned immutable VICE behavior for the same selected machine, tape media state, control sequence, and emulated clock sequence. Machine-specific tape-sense and pulse wiring belong in machine adapters. Internal pulse-buffer success or compatibility with managed-only tests does not establish VICE parity.
result.title: Datasette motor ramp + sense line + record mode

acceptanceCriteria.text: Drive STOP, START, FORWARD, REWIND, and RECORD from a known STOP state with no image, read-only image, and writable image. Each accepted mode and tape-sense transition matches pinned VICE. No-image RECORD and read-only-image RECORD leave mode and sense unchanged; accepted RECORD with writable media asserts sense.

For identical accepted tape-sense transitions, C64 CPU port $0001 input bit 4 and VIC-20 VIA1 port A input bit 6 match pinned VICE, including input/output direction masking. C64 CIA1 FLAG and VIC-20 VIA2 CA1 pulse events are tested separately and are not substituted for tape-sense input.

With an initially stopped motor and no pending datasette alarm, a motor-on transition schedules the startup read alarm at the current emulated clock plus 32000. The ordered read-side event trace immediately before, at, and after that deadline matches pinned VICE. A pre-existing pending alarm is preserved as VICE preserves it; metadata retrieval alone is not counted as a pulse event.

For a running motor, motor-off schedules stopping at current clock plus 32000 without stopping immediately. Motor-on before that stop executes cancels the pending stop without imposing a new startup ramp. Repeated motor-off does not extend an existing stop deadline. Ordered boundary events and restart after an executed stop match pinned VICE.

Recording writes occur only under the native combination of an attached image, accepted RECORD mode, running motor, and qualifying write-line transition. No image, read-only media that rejected RECORD, wrong mode, motor stopped, repeated levels, and nonqualifying transitions produce the same absence of tape writes as pinned VICE.

For identical accepted recording signal traces and media, emitted TAP bytes, elapsed-gap/remainder handling, first-write state, image-position updates, and failure/STOP side effects match pinned VICE. Cover short and long gap boundaries and partial or failed writes; an incremented managed pulse-buffer count alone does not satisfy this criterion.

result.body: Model accepted VICE transport state and image eligibility before deriving tape sense or recording eligibility. Preserve the distinction between device sense state, each machine input port, and tape read-pulse interrupt wiring. Recording consumes ordered clocked write-line transitions and retains the native gap, image-position, and write-failure behavior through the managed adapter.
result.title: Datasette sense line and record mode

acceptanceCriteria.text: Use the FR-RUNTIME-TAPE-002 ac-01 media/control matrix to assert accepted mode, sense state, and unchanged state for ignored RECORD commands; do not treat an unconstrained RecordPressed flag as proof that RECORD was accepted.

Use FR-RUNTIME-TAPE-002 ac-02 observations to assert the C64 CPU-port and VIC-20 VIA1 input bits for both data-direction settings; separately assert pulse routing to C64 CIA1 FLAG and VIC-20 VIA2 CA1.

Use the same recording eligibility traces as FR-RUNTIME-TAPE-002 ac-05. Assert emitted writes and absence of writes as well as updated last-write-line state, including input transitions while recording is ineligible.

Use the same recording byte/error traces as FR-RUNTIME-TAPE-002 ac-06. Preserve the pinned native first-write handling and encoded gap behavior, including known native quirks, without patching VICE or replacing expected values with managed output.

result.body: Represent datasette startup and delayed motor-stop state in emulated-clock units, preserving pinned VICE alarm scheduling and event order. Preserve pending alarms, cancel a pending stop when motor is re-enabled before the stop executes, and distinguish motor control input from the running-motor state. The observable timing contract must not depend on whether a particular managed Tick method has already been called.
result.title: Datasette motor 32,000-cycle ramp before pulse delivery

acceptanceCriteria.text: Assert the native startup schedule at t+32000 from a stopped motor with no pending alarm, and assert that a pending alarm is not overwritten by the start helper.
Assert motor-off at t on a running motor retains running state before the stop executes at t+32000, and that repeated motor-off preserves the first deadline.

Assert motor-on before pending stop execution clears the stop deadline and preserves running state without another startup delay; assert motor-on after an executed stop schedules a new native startup alarm.

Compare ordered pulse and motor-state traces at deadline-1, deadline, and deadline+1 using fixed clock/control/alarm order. Do not use a first-Tick bypass or an unconditional off/on ramp reset as a substitute for native behavior.

result.condition: Validate FR-RUNTIME-TAPE-002 ac-03/ac-04 and every TR-TAPE-EDGE-001 criterion using shared clock/control/alarm fixtures. First prove correct and deliberately incorrect mock traces discriminate in an entirely passing native-safe suite. Then bind unchanged fixtures and assertions to managed behavior and immutable native VICE observations. Preserve historical results but remove fixed historical pass-count claims from the acceptance condition.
result.title: Datasette motor startup and delayed-stop parity

acceptanceCriteria.text: Named cases Startup_NoPendingAlarm_DeadlineBoundaries and Startup_PendingAlarm_NotOverwritten assert complete ordered event traces; incorrect early, late, missing, duplicated, and reordered events are rejected within a passing mock harness.

Named cases MotorOff_DelayedStop, MotorOff_RepeatedDoesNotExtend, MotorOn_CancelsPendingStop, and MotorOn_AfterExecutedStop_Restarts assert state and event order at deadline-1, deadline, and deadline+1. A mock implementing immediate stop or unconditional off/on restart must be rejected.

The real-provider run reuses every mock-case input and assertion and compares actual native and managed clocked observations. A pure pulse-duration getter or source inspection is not accepted as a machine-visible pulse trace.

All cases execute without skips in the full applicable cumulative suite after native-safe harness integration. Retain exact commands, counts, TRX/logs, native input identities, failure history, and hostile validation; no count-only or mock-only result marks these criteria satisfied.

result.condition: Validate FR-RUNTIME-TAPE-002 ac-01/ac-02/ac-05/ac-06 and every TR-TAP-EDGE-001 criterion with shared media, accepted transport-command, machine-port, and write-line fixtures. Establish correct and discriminating incorrect mocks before product changes, then reuse the same cases and assertions against managed and immutable native providers. result.title: Datasette transport, sense wiring and recording parity

acceptanceCriteria.text: TransportSense_MediaCommandMatrix covers the five transport commands from STOP for absent/read-only/writable media and subsequent STOP transitions. Correct mocks assert accepted mode and sense; wrong polarity, ignored-command state changes, and omitted transitions are rejected.

MachineSense_C64CpuPortAndVic20Via1 covers both machines and input/output masking. TapeRead_PulseInterruptRouting separately verifies CIA1 FLAG and VIA2 CA1. Wrong port, bit, DDR handling, interrupt target, and extra interrupts are rejected by negative controls.

Recording_EligibilityAndWriteEdges covers attached versus absent media, RECORD accepted versus rejected, running versus stopped motor, and qualifying versus repeated/opposite write levels. Correct mocks assert writes and no-writes plus state changes; the historical no-tape successful-write behavior must be rejected.

Recording_GapEncodingAndFailures covers elapsed gaps 0,6,7,8,2046,2047, short-gap remainder carry, first-write state, TAP v0/v1/v2 paths supported by the pinned source, and first/partial/failed output writes. Assert emitted bytes, image position, dirty state and STOP side effects against independently pinned expectations.

Real-provider validation reuses all fixtures and assertions with actual immutable VICE and managed observations, followed by the full cumulative native-safe and real-emulator gates. Preserve historical tests/evidence, explicitly record superseded wrong expectations, and require zero failed, skipped or aborted cases plus accepted hostile validation before satisfaction.

result.body:
The Commodore Datasette tape drive motor is controlled by bit 3 of the 6510 I/O port ($0001). The motor is active-low (writing 0 turns the motor on). The motor has a spin-up delay before tape movement begins and a mechanical inertia effect.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Bit 3 of $0001 controls the motor: 0 = motor on, 1 = motor off.
- The motor spin-up delay (approximately 0.5 seconds on real hardware) is modeled.
- The tape position advances only when the motor is running and spin-up is complete.
- The PLAY button state (bit 4 of $0001, cassette sense) must be active (low) for the motor to engage.
- Motor state changes are reflected in the `ITapeUnit.MotorState` property.
- Audio output from the tape (when connected to SID EXT IN) is modeled.

result.body:
The TAP file format stores raw tape pulse timing data. TAP v0 stores pulse lengths as single bytes (with 0 indicating an overflow requiring 3 additional bytes). TAP v1 extends the overflow encoding. The emulator shall read and write both TAP format versions.

## Acceptance Criteria
- TAP v0 files are correctly parsed: each byte represents a pulse half-period in units of 8 system clock cycles.
- A byte value of 0 in TAP v0 indicates the next 3 bytes form a 24-bit little-endian overflow value.
- TAP v1 files use an extended header and the same pulse encoding with improved overflow handling.
- The TAP header (magic bytes, version, platform, video standard, data length) is validated on load.
- Tape images can be mounted and unmounted at runtime via `ITapeUnit.Mount()`/`ITapeUnit.Eject()`.
- Writing to TAP format captures the pulse timing from emulated writes.
- The platform byte in the header distinguishes C64, VIC-20, and C16/Plus4 tapes.

result.body:
Tape reading relies on the CIA1 Timer A or the FLAG pin to measure the time between pulses from the datasette. The Kernal tape routine uses Timer A in one-shot mode to measure pulse widths and classify them as short, medium, or long pulses for data decoding.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Each pulse from the tape triggers the FLAG input on CIA1 (directly connected to the cassette read line).
- The time between pulses is measured by CIA1 Timer A and/or by CIA1 FLAG interrupts.
- Standard Commodore encoding uses three pulse widths: short (352 cycles TAP value $30), medium (512 cycles TAP value $42), and long (672 cycles TAP value $56).
- The standard Commodore tape header (FOUND marker), data blocks, and checksums are readable.
- Tape reading at normal speed produces identical results to real hardware.
- The timing accuracy supports both PAL and NTSC system clock rates.

result.body:
The emulator shall support writing data to tape images via the datasette write line. The write signal from the VIA/CIA generates pulses that are recorded to the TAP file with correct timing.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The tape write line output generates pulses whose timing is captured.
- Written pulses are stored in TAP format with correct timing values.
- The standard Commodore SAVE routine produces valid tape data.
- Writes can be appended to existing TAP files or written to new files.
- The record interlock (RECORD + PLAY buttons) must be engaged for writes.

result.body:
The MOS 6510 processor's built-in I/O port at addresses $0000 (data direction register) and $0001 (data port) shall be emulated. This port controls the PLA memory banking configuration (LORAM, HIRAM, CHAREN bits), the cassette motor, and the cassette sense line. The data port shall exhibit the correct behavior with pull-up/pull-down resistors and the capacitive discharge timing that affects reads of output pins.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Address $0000 is the Data Direction Register (DDR); bits set to 1 configure the corresponding $0001 bit as output.
- Address $0001 bits 0-2 (LORAM, HIRAM, CHAREN) control PLA banking and are reflected immediately in the address space configuration.
- Bit 3 controls the cassette motor (active low).
- Bit 4 reads the cassette switch sense (active low).
- Bit 5 is unused on C64 but reads as expected based on DDR/pull-up behavior.
- When a bit transitions from output to input, the capacitive discharge timing (approximately 350 microseconds to decay) is modeled.
- The `IMemoryMappedDevice` interface exposes the port to the address decoder.

result.body:
The SX-64 is a portable C64 with a built-in 1541 disk drive and a 5" color monitor. It lacks a cassette port and has a different KERNAL ROM (no tape routines, different screen colors on startup).

## Acceptance Criteria
- KERNAL: SX-64 variant KERNAL ROM with different default colors (blue screen instead of light blue).
- No cassette port: tape-related I/O port bits behave differently (cassette sense always reads "no tape").
- Built-in 1541 drive: device 8 is always present.
- The 6510 I/O port bit 4 (cassette sense) is permanently pulled high.
- All other hardware is identical to the C64 NMOS profile.
- Selectable via `IMachineProfile.LoadProfile("sx64")`.

result.body:
Many commercial C64 programs used turbo tape loaders that employ faster pulse encoding than the standard Commodore format. The emulator shall support turbo loaders by providing accurate tape read timing down to individual clock cycles.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Turbo loaders using shorter pulse widths than standard (down to approximately 160 cycles per pulse) function correctly.
- Common turbo formats (Novaload, Biturbo, Turbotape, Cyberload, Pavloda) load successfully.
- Custom pulse encoding schemes are supported through accurate pulse-level emulation.
- The CIA FLAG input timing is accurate to 1 system clock cycle.
- Half-wave and full-wave detection methods both work correctly.
- Multi-speed loaders (that change pulse rates mid-load) are supported.

originalProjectedFieldComparisons.expected:
The TAP file format stores raw tape pulse timing data. TAP v0 stores pulse lengths as single bytes (with 0 indicating an overflow requiring 3 additional bytes). TAP v1 extends the overflow encoding. The emulator shall read and write both TAP format versions.

## Acceptance Criteria
- TAP v0 files are correctly parsed: each byte represents a pulse half-period in units of 8 system clock cycles.
- A byte value of 0 in TAP v0 indicates the next 3 bytes form a 24-bit little-endian overflow value.
- TAP v1 files use an extended header and the same pulse encoding with improved overflow handling.
- The TAP header (magic bytes, version, platform, video standard, data length) is validated on load.
- Tape images can be mounted and unmounted at runtime via `ITapeUnit.Mount()`/`ITapeUnit.Eject()`.
- Writing to TAP format captures the pulse timing from emulated writes.
- The platform byte in the header distinguishes C64, VIC-20, and C16/Plus4 tapes.

originalProjectedFieldComparisons.expected:
Tape reading relies on the CIA1 Timer A or the FLAG pin to measure the time between pulses from the datasette. The Kernal tape routine uses Timer A in one-shot mode to measure pulse widths and classify them as short, medium, or long pulses for data decoding.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Each pulse from the tape triggers the FLAG input on CIA1 (directly connected to the cassette read line).
- The time between pulses is measured by CIA1 Timer A and/or by CIA1 FLAG interrupts.
- Standard Commodore encoding uses three pulse widths: short (352 cycles TAP value $30), medium (512 cycles TAP value $42), and long (672 cycles TAP value $56).
- The standard Commodore tape header (FOUND marker), data blocks, and checksums are readable.
- Tape reading at normal speed produces identical results to real hardware.
- The timing accuracy supports both PAL and NTSC system clock rates.

originalProjectedFieldComparisons.expected:
The MOS 6510 processor's built-in I/O port at addresses $0000 (data direction register) and $0001 (data port) shall be emulated. This port controls the PLA memory banking configuration (LORAM, HIRAM, CHAREN bits), the cassette motor, and the cassette sense line. The data port shall exhibit the correct behavior with pull-up/pull-down resistors and the capacitive discharge timing that affects reads of output pins.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Address $0000 is the Data Direction Register (DDR); bits set to 1 configure the corresponding $0001 bit as output.
- Address $0001 bits 0-2 (LORAM, HIRAM, CHAREN) control PLA banking and are reflected immediately in the address space configuration.
- Bit 3 controls the cassette motor (active low).
- Bit 4 reads the cassette switch sense (active low).
- Bit 5 is unused on C64 but reads as expected based on DDR/pull-up behavior.
- When a bit transitions from output to input, the capacitive discharge timing (approximately 350 microseconds to decay) is modeled.
- The `IMemoryMappedDevice` interface exposes the port to the address decoder.

The SX-64 is a portable C64 with a built-in 1541 disk drive and a 5" color monitor. It lacks a cassette port and has a different KERNAL ROM (no tape routines, different screen colors on startup).

## Acceptance Criteria
- KERNAL: SX-64 variant KERNAL ROM with different default colors (blue screen instead of light blue).
- No cassette port: tape-related I/O port bits behave differently (cassette sense always reads "no tape").
- Built-in 1541 drive: device 8 is always present.
- The 6510 I/O port bit 4 (cassette sense) is permanently pulled high.
- All other hardware is identical to the C64 NMOS profile.
- Selectable via `IMachineProfile.LoadProfile("sx64")`.

Many commercial C64 programs used turbo tape loaders that employ faster pulse encoding than the standard Commodore format. The emulator shall support turbo loaders by providing accurate tape read timing down to individual clock cycles.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Turbo loaders using shorter pulse widths than standard (down to approximately 160 cycles per pulse) function correctly.
- Common turbo formats (Novaload, Biturbo, Turbotape, Cyberload, Pavloda) load successfully.
- Custom pulse encoding schemes are supported through accurate pulse-level emulation.
- The CIA FLAG input timing is accurate to 1 system clock cycle.
- Half-wave and full-wave detection methods both work correctly.
- Multi-speed loaders (that change pulse rates mid-load) are supported.
